**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/24 (Wed) 16:35  
[USER] User asked about linear transformation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A linear transformation is a function between vector spaces that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If T is a linear transformation and u and v are vectors in the domain of T, and a is a scalar, then T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v) and T(au) = aT(u).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Linear transformations can be represented by matrices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The set of all linear transformations from a vector space V to a vector space W forms a vector space, known as the space of linear transformations from V to W.  
[USER] User did not understand the explanation and requested a simpler explanation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A linear transformation is a way of changing or moving a set of points in a special way, like moving dots on paper to create a new picture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It involves instructions like moving a dot a certain number of steps in specific directions, making it bigger, or turning it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is called "linear" because it only makes the dots move in straight lines.  
[USER] User found the explanation somewhat clear and requested a real-world example.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A real-world example of a linear transformation is stretching or shrinking an image on a computer screen by multiplying each pixel's coordinates by a scaling factor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Another example is rotating an object in 3D space, which can be represented as a linear transformation matrix.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A third example is projecting a 3D object onto a 2D plane, like a shadow, by transforming 3D coordinates into 2D coordinates.  
[USER] User requested more intuition about the third example.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Projecting a 3D object onto a 2D plane is like casting a shadow of a 3D object onto a flat surface, showing only the shape without depth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This process is a linear transformation because it changes the position of points in straight lines.  
[USER] User asked for a real-world example of this projection.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example is in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software, where 3D models are projected onto 2D drawings for construction and fabrication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Linear transformations are also used in robotics, computer vision, and machine learning.  
[USER] User asked how linear transformations are used in machine learning.
